chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Among My believing servants are servants whose affairs of their religion cannot be rectified for them except through wealth, abundance, and health in the body. So I test them with wealth, abundance, and health of the body, so that I may rectify their religious affairs for them.'

And among My believing servants are servants whose affairs of their religion cannot be rectified for them except through poverty, destitution, and sickness in their bodies. So I test them with poverty, destitution, and sickness, so that I may rectify their religious affairs for them. And I am the One Who knows best what rectifies the religious affairs of My believing servants.

And among My believing servants is one who strives in My worship, rising from his sleep and the pleasure of his pillow, staying awake for Me through the nights, thus tiring himself in My worship. So I strike him with drowsiness for the night and the two nights, as a consideration from Me to him and a preservation for him, so he sleeps until morning. Then he rises, and he is disgusted with himself, fretting over it.

And if I were to leave him alone to do what he intends from My worship, self-conceit would enter him because of that. So self-conceit would lead him to trial through his deeds, and there would come to him from that that which causes his destruction due to his conceit in his deeds and his satisfaction with himself, until he thinks that he has surpassed the worshippers and exceeded the limit of deficiency in his worship. Thus, he becomes distant from Me at that time, while he thinks he is drawing near to Me.

So let the workers not rely upon their deeds which they perform for My reward. For if they strive and tire themselves and spend their lives in My worship, they would be deficient, not reaching the full measure of their worship in what they seek from Me of My generosity, the bliss in My Paradise, and the high ranks in My vicinity. But (they attain it) by My Mercy.

So let them have trust in My grace, let them rejoice, and let them be assured in their good opinion of Me. For My Mercy will overtake them at that time, and from Me, My Pleasure will reach them, and My Forgiveness will clothe them in My Pardoning. Indeed, I am Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and with that I am Named.'
ai.seo_question: How does Allah test believers with wealth versus poverty, and why does He strike worshippers with drowsiness?
ai.summary: This Hadith Qudsi, recorded in al-Kafi, elucidates the divine wisdom behind varying states of wealth, health, and fatigue, framing them as precise instruments for spiritual refinement rather than arbitrary trials. It highlights the subtle danger of 'al-'ujb' (self-conceit) in diligent worshipers, illustrating how Allah’s mercy often manifests through interruption or ease to preserve humility. The narration concludes by anchoring ultimate salvation in divine grace (rahmah) rather than the sheer volume of deeds, a core tenet of Shia theological optimism regarding God's boundless generosity.
